title: Orion: A Fully Homomorphic Encryption Framework for Deep Learning
problem: Mapping arbitrary deep neural networks to Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) primitives is intractable with existing tools because FHE requires packing large vectors, managing noise budget through bootstrap placement, and translating general convolutions to the limited FHE instruction set—challenges that have limited FHE neural inference to shallow or small networks.
motivation: Neural network inference in the cloud exposes user data to service providers; FHE enables inference on encrypted inputs, but the lack of automated, scalable compilation frameworks has prevented deployment of large models (e.g., ResNet-50, YOLO).
method: Orion is an automated compiler that translates deep neural networks from PyTorch into programs that compute directly on encrypted data (fully homomorphic encryption). The core problem is that encrypted computation requires packing numbers into encrypted slots, and different packing arrangements cause combinatorial explosion—Orion's single-shot multiplexed packing strategy efficiently handles arbitrary convolutions without generating all those possibilities. It also automatically decides where to insert bootstrap operations (which refresh the noise budget in encrypted computation) by tracking noise accumulation across layers and placing bootstraps where they cost the least. This approach enables end-to-end compilation of large networks including ResNet-20, ResNet-50, and YOLO-v1 (139 million parameters) without manual FHE engineering.
key_novelty: Orion combines a single-shot multiplexed packing strategy for arbitrary convolutions with automated bootstrap placement that minimizes noise-refresh costs, enabling fully automatic compilation of large convolutional neural networks to fully homomorphic encryption (computation on encrypted data).
contributions: Single-shot multiplexed packing strategy for FHE-mapping of arbitrary convolutions.
Automated bootstrap placement and noise/scale management algorithm for deep networks.
Orion open-source framework accepting PyTorch models and emitting FHE programs.
First high-resolution FHE object detection (YOLO-v1, 139M parameters) and FHE ResNet-50 on ImageNet; 2.38x speedup over state-of-the-art on ResNet-20.

metrics.other: First FHE YOLO-v1 (139M params) and FHE ResNet-50 on ImageNet reported

baselines: prior FHE DL frameworks (state-of-the-art on ResNet-20)
limitations: FHE inference remains orders of magnitude slower than plaintext inference; Orion improves relative to prior FHE work but absolute latency is not discussed for practical deployment.
primary_theme: automated FHE compilation for deep learning inference
